name: Sean Hacking
headline: Mechanical engineer. I take hardware from a rough sketch to a tested prototype to production.
intro: I design mechanisms, build the prototypes and test them until they hold up. I founded and ran a hardware company that shipped 10,000+ units, and most recently worked on Zipline's New Products team.
about:
I'm a mechanical engineer who gets hardware from a napkin sketch to a flight-tested prototype to production, quickly.

Most recently I was on Zipline's New Products team, where I took the second-generation drone-loading kiosk through 9 flight-tested prototypes across 3 generations. Before that I founded Veer, a cycling drivetrain company that grew from zero to $1.4M in revenue and shipped 10,000+ units to 16 OEMs. After Veer I set up Form Robotics, a prototyping shop built around five CNC machines.

I like owning whole systems: the mechanism, the test rig that proves it, and the cost and supplier work that gets it shipped. I'm a named inventor on 6+ patents, granted or pending. When something keeps failing, I find out why and fix the design.

I studied bioengineering at UC Santa Cruz and started out building liquid-handling robots for synthetic DNA manufacturing.

## Working together

I take on mechanical engineering projects: a prototype from sketch to tested hardware, a DFM and cost-down push, a test rig, or a mechanism that keeps failing. The [contact page](/contact/) has the ways to reach me.

experience.role: Senior Mechanical Engineer, New Products Team
highlights: Developed the second-generation Zipline Dropbox (robotic drone loading and package pickup kiosk) from rough sketches through 9 flight-tested prototypes across 3 generations.
Sole R&D engineer through early architecture, then owned all systems interacting with the active package (Droid/Pod) on the design team.
Invented and developed multiple critical systems that defined the kiosk architecture: >10x improvement in key package-pickup reliability metrics.
~3x cost reduction versus the current production generation through architecture decisions and DFM.
Named inventor on at least one patent application.
Ran prototypes through lab and flight testing on tight cycles; worked with electrical, software, NPI and supply chain toward production.
Built a prototyping facility with 5 CNC machines from scratch: same-day design-to-testable-part.
Invented the LavaLock universal workholding system: 91% setup-time reduction, 50% prototype cost savings; developed a custom thermoplastic resin (561 PSI vs. 300 PSI commercial).
Machined next-day prototypes for aerospace and robotics customers, including Zipline motor housings and bulkheads.
MVP and early sales within 6 months.
Hardware startup from zero to $1.4M revenue; raised $2M; built and led a team of 8 (3 mechanical engineers); in-house CNC production; managed 4 key manufacturing vendors.
Shipped 10,000+ drivetrain units to 16 OEMs, 3 international distributors and 43 dealers.

Invented and commercialised Split Belt Pro and the V-Link detachable belt splice, creating the first belt-drive conversion category for cycling; won the Eurobike Startup Award competing against Gates.

Invented the SHIFT seamless belt transmission (shifts under load without a clutch); wrote and prosecuted the patent to grant in the US and internationally with no rejections; hit a $30 unit-cost target at 100K volume through DFM.

Built a drivetrain test suite exceeding ISO standards on a shoestring (a UTM from a log splitter and load cell, $500 and 1 week); root-caused early belt failures and redesigned to a 20,000-mile lifespan.
Designed and programmed the LinkBot automated belt-assembly tool: installation from 10 min to under 30 s, under 1 fault per 4,000 rivets, delivered to 3 OEMs on a $10K / 4-month budget.
Created 70+ pulley designs and an accessory catalogue for drop-in fitment across millions of vehicles.
Built and programmed custom liquid-handling robotics for synthetic DNA manufacturing; 93% microsphere enrichment.
Invented the first process for recovering monoclonal DNA clusters from Illumina flow cells; designed precision components for DNA laser-catapult systems.
